content.title: About
content.content: Rice, white, cooked, fat added is boiled white rice to which a plant or animal fat (oil, butter, margarine) has been incorporated during cooking. This product is commonly used to enhance flavor and increase the energy value of dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice loses most of its fiber and micronutrients during milling, but remains a good source of carbohydrates.
Adding fat improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as A and D when they are present in the meal.
In many Asian cuisines rice is cooked with oil or coconut milk to make it richer and more satisfying.
Cooking rice with fat reduces stickiness, resulting in more separate grains.
Rice is a staple food for more than half of the world’s population.

items.title: Energy density
items.content: The added fat raises the calorie content, which can be beneficial for individuals with high energy needs.

items.title: Improved satiety and taste
items.content: Fats enhance flavor and promote a longer feeling of fullness.

items.title: Better absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins
items.content: Presence of fat helps the body absorb vitamins A, D, E and K more efficiently if they are part of the dish.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides a quick source of glucose, essential for brain and muscle energy.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Boiled rice is gentle on the digestive system, making it suitable for diets with gastrointestinal concerns.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The added fat significantly increases calories, which may contribute to weight gain if consumed in excess.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Using butter or palm oil can raise saturated fat levels, which is undesirable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice has a high glycemic index and can cause rapid blood sugar spikes, especially in people with diabetes.

items.title: Allergy to added oils
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to certain plant oils.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rice with added fat can be served as a side dish with meat, fish or vegetables, used in pilaf, fried rice, sushi, or as a base for salads. Garnish with fresh herbs, spices or sauces for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to at least 75 °C before consumption.
